prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. BODY PLAN BASE BODY sheet for a modular creature kit: Giant humanoid body plan (Biped spine, two arms, two legs). One base body shared by The Drowned Colossus 25 m and The Stormmother 50 m at the shoulder; draw it about 30 m tall, so the 1.8 m human figure is tiny, standing at its feet. A plain bare featureless giant torso with plain arms and legs, no head (a neck socket ring), smooth plain skin. Mark exactly these sockets as small numbered rings with short labels: 1 head (ring at the neck), 2 crown or mask (a small ring just above the neck ring, labelled 'fits on the head'), 3 arms (rings at the left and right shoulders), 4 carried ruins (rings on the upper back and the top of each shoulder), 5 storm growths (rings along the spine and on each forearm). Do not mark any other socket. Draw one neutral, featureless base body (no head detail, no horns, no ears, no tail tip, smooth plain skin) in a relaxed standing pose with the limbs apart and clear of the body, shown as front, side, back and top views in orthographic projection. Mark every socket where a swappable part attaches as a small numbered ring with a short label (for example "1 head", "2 horns", "3 tail"). Thick, solid forms; even proportions that can be stretched to make larger or smaller species. Only the base body and its socket labels: no parts, heads, horns, coats or tails anywhere on this sheet, because the parts have their own sheet. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Body plan: giant humanoid".
